summary: Chats from before pull request linking existed get linked too. Once per chat, shortly after launch, the backend reads the chat's stored history from the sources a chat is opened from (the SQLite message mirror row by row, then the Claude and Codex JSONL transcripts line by line through JsonlParser, plus the tool results and Codex tool calls that parser drops) and applies the live auto-link rule (autoLinkRefs) to its user text, assistant text, tool inputs and tool output, so a PR URL pasted by the user, passed to a CLI (`bbpr https://bitbucket.org/ws/repo/pull-requests/605 diff`) or printed by one is linked. A bbpr command with a bare number in a tool input (`bbpr 605`, `cd <dir> && bbpr 605 diff`; only a command that invokes bbpr, never a number elsewhere) names PR 605 of the chat's project repository, for a Bitbucket project only (src/shared/bbpr-command.ts). Only PRs of the repository the chat's project points at are linked, an unlinked tombstone is never revived, and each PR links once. The read stops at 250,000 characters per chat (text repeated by two sources counts once), so a huge chat is never loaded whole; a URL or number the cap cuts in half is not matched, and a chat with more text after the cap is reported as partly read. The scan runs in batches of 50 with two chats at a time and a 25 ms pause between chats, records each chat it has read in the new conversation_pr_history_scans table so it never reads it again, and pages past a chat whose record could not be written instead of stopping; later messages are the live auto-linker's. 'Find linked PRs in this chat' on a local chat's sidebar context menu re-scans that one chat on demand and says how many PRs it linked and whether the chat was only partly read.

reactNativeIos.reason: The phone app does not show chat to PR links yet (they come with the Reviews tab behind mobile_reviews, see reviews-to-chat.json). Links the scan adds are stored on the backend under the chat's root conversation and read through the unchanged pull-requests:links and pull-requests:linked-chats channels, so the Reviews tab will see them with no further change. No manual scan action on the phone.

nativeAndroid.reason: Same as the React Native app: native Android has no linking UI yet (Reviews destination behind native_reviews), and scanned links reach it through the existing pull-requests:links channels. No manual scan action on Android.

updateRelease.reason: One additive channel (pull-requests:history-scan) and one additive table created with CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS; an older build ignores the table, and a newer build against an older backend only loses the menu action (the invoke fails and the dialog says it could not scan). No package identity, signing, deep-link or update channel change.

automated: tests/unit/pull-request-history-scan.test.ts: a bbpr-style Bitbucket URL in stored tool output links the PR and notifies clients; a PR URL in a tool input links; a bare `bbpr 605` in a tool input links PR 605 of a Bitbucket project, but not in chat text or tool output and not on a GitHub project; user text is scanned and a PR of another repository is not linked; a refused (tombstoned) link adds nothing; a scanned chat is not read again; the read stops at the cap and says capped, also when text follows a part that fills the cap exactly (and not when nothing follows); a URL or bbpr number cut by the cap is not linked; text repeated by two sources counts once; the pending scan works through every batch, pages past a chat that could not be marked, and keeps going when a chat can be neither read nor marked; historyScanSummary wording.

tests/unit/bbpr-command.test.ts: bbpr at the start, after &&, ||, ;, | and a newline, after `cd "<dir>" &&`, with a path prefix; ignored as a later argument, after echo, in a comment, inside quotes, as part of another word, or with a non-number first argument. toolInputCommand reads Claude Bash input, Codex argv and a bare command.

tests/unit/pull-request-history-source.test.ts (real temp files): a Claude transcript yields user text, assistant text, the tool input and the tool_result text the parser drops; a Codex transcript yields its function_call arguments and output; reading a 5,000-line file stops once the visitor says so; a missing file reads as empty.
tests/unit/pull-request-links-db.test.ts: marking a chat through a rotated session id records the root conversation, and the unscanned list skips rotated aliases and terminals.
npm run typecheck and npm test green.
notExercised: The background scan and the sidebar menu item were not run in the built app against a real database with pre-linking chats; the scan logic is covered through injected dependencies and the transcript reader through temp files. readConversationHistory's source discovery (thread family, session hints, segments, profile dirs, Codex rollouts) is not unit-tested; it uses the same helpers as loadConversationHistory.
Main-thread cost of the first scan over a large collection of chats is bounded by the cap, batch size, concurrency 2 and the pause between chats, but not measured.
A bbpr command run in a directory other than the project (`cd ../other && bbpr 605`) is still attributed to the chat's project repository.
